If underreporting is limited to the richest households, then the attribution of the entire discrepancy between national accounts and surveys to missing top incomes remains valid. A more measured approach would be to attribute a portion of the discrepancy between national accounts and surveys to missing top incomes. Generate Form 15CA & 15CB in Bulk Published on 5 April 2025 Understanding Income Underreporting and Misreporting: Transfer Pricing Insights Underreporting and Misreporting of Income: A Comprehensive Overview on Transfer Pricing Adjustments The Finance Bill 2016 introduced significant changes to the penalty regime within income tax law, inducing concerns among taxpayers. Previously, the Income Tax Act of 1961 stipulated penalties for concealing income or providing inaccurate income particulars under section 271(1)(c), ranging from 100% to 300% of the evaded tax. The new framework established under section 270A of the Income Tax Act categorizes income variations into two classes: 'underreporting' and 'misreporting.' Penalties for underreporting are set at 50% of the tax base, while misreporting penalties are pegged at 200%. The Faceless Assessing Officer, Jurisdictional Assessing Officer, Commissioner (Appeals), Principal Commissioner, or Commissioner may, during proceedings, assess penalties for underreported income. According to Sub-section (6) of Section 270A, certain situations exclude the assessment of underreported income, provided the taxpayer discloses material facts. * **Self Disallowances:** Cases where the taxpayer has self-disallowed income (e.g., under section 14A), and the Assessing Officer increases this disallowance. Section 270A(1) enables the tax authority to impose penalties on individuals who underreport income, which includes income discrepancies resulting from misreporting. Hence, 'underreporting' incorporates instances of 'misreporting.' Distinction Between Underreporting and Misreporting * Underreporting involves failing to declare the total income properly. * Underreporting can incur penalties up to 50% of the tax due. Immunity from Penalty under section 270A Under Section 270AA, taxpayers may apply to the Assessing Officer within one month to seek immunity from penalties under section 270A. This section delineates clear terms for penalties regarding underreporting and misreporting, requiring taxpayers to maintain thorough documentation and transparency. Taxpayers should ensure compliance with documentation requirements under Section 92D and Rule 10D of the Income Tax Rules, 1961.
